# Standard Practice
These procedures apply during every shift, whether or not an incident is in progress.
## Appearance - Officers are to be in full uniform and issued kit on duty. - An officer who looks professional is rarely asked to prove it.
## Patrols - The Sergeant assigns patrol routes at the start of the shift. The laboratory and the corporate offices are always covered. - Patrols check that restricted doors are locked, that nobody is where they shouldn't be, and that Company property is where it should be. - Anything out of place is reported to the Sergeant.
## Access Control - Only Company staff may enter Company areas. Visitors may enter only with the senior employee's permission and must be escorted at all times. - Research areas are open only to research staff, Security and the senior employee on site. - Anyone found in a restricted area without permission is to be detained and questioned.
## Searches - Anyone entering or leaving a restricted area may be searched. - Company property found on a person is recovered and logged. - Recording devices found on non-Company personnel are confiscated.
## Detention - Persons of interest may be [italic]invited[/italic] to the Company offices to answer questions. Most accept. Those who don't may be restrained. - Detainees are to be given food and water and no reason to complain afterwards. - A detainee is released only when the senior employee on site is satisfied. - Detention is logged with the time, the reason and the officer responsible.
## Use of Force - Force is to be proportionate to the threat to the Company, not only to the officer. - Non-lethal options (batons, restraints, tear gas and flashbangs) are to be used first wherever they will do the job. - Armed persons who have shown intent to use their weapon may be met with lethal force. - Trespassers in the laboratory may be shot with little or no warning if it is needed to stop confidential material leaving. - All use of force is reported to the Sergeant, who reports it to the senior employee.
## Colonial Law Enforcement - Colonial law applies on colonial ground. Where the colony's marshals are present, they are to be seen to act. - Officers are to be courteous to colonial law enforcement and are not to obstruct them openly. - Colonial law enforcement may not be given access to Company areas without the senior employee's permission.
## Reporting - Every incident is reported to the Sergeant in writing. - The Sergeant reports to the senior employee, and to nobody else. - No incident may be discussed with anyone outside the Company. Questions are to be referred to the Corporate Liaison.
